function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that you’ll need to add to the repository.

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually clone or push to the remote for you, but the commands below will do it for you once you run them locally.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# Clone the repo into a folder called nodejs-welcome
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the required artefacts

> The repo is a tiny Node.js “Hello World” app that listens on port **3000**.  
> (If the repo structure is different, adjust the files accordingly.)

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the root of the repo with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Use the official Node.js 18 image (Alpine for a small footprint)
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install app dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install --production

# Bundle app source
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and contains everything you need to run a Node.js app.  
> * We copy only the `package*.json` first so that Docker can cache the `npm install` step.  
> * The app is started with `node app.js` – change this if your entry point is different.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s.yaml` (or split into `deployment.yaml` & `service.yaml`) with the following content:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- this will be built by the GitHub Action
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 3000
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes port 3000 inside the cluster.  
> * Creates a `ClusterIP` service that other pods can reach via `nodejs-welcome-service`.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a directory `.github/workflows` (if it doesn’t exist) and add a file named `docker-build.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Docker Buildx (needed for multi‑platform builds)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      # Log in to Docker Hub (or GitHub Container Registry)
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the image and push it to Docker Hub
      - name: Build & push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: yourdockerhubusername/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Important**  
> * Replace `yourdockerhubusername` with your actual Docker Hub username.  
> * Add two repository secrets in GitHub:  
>   * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub login name  
>   * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or password).  
> * If you prefer GitHub Container Registry, change the login step to `docker/login-action@v2` with `registry: ghcr.io` and adjust the tag accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣ Stage the new files

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once the push completes, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the Docker image, and push it to Docker Hub. The Kubernetes YAML can then be applied to any cluster with:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s.yaml
```

---

### Quick sanity check

After the workflow finishes, verify that the image exists:

```bash
docker pull yourdockerhubusername/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

And test the deployment locally (optional):

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s.yaml
kubectl get pods
kubectl port-forward svc/nodejs-welcome-service 3000:3000
curl http://localhost:3000
```

That’s it! 🎉 If you hit any snags, let me know and I’ll help troubleshoot.
